overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the member's reopening proposal was not shared with a quorum outside a posted meeting, and the unanticipated topic did not require separate notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged members may have deliberated outside a posted meeting about a member's school reopening plan presented at the August 6 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Member Visnick did not share her proposal with a quorum of Committee members outside of a posted meeting, nor did a quorum of the Committee learn about the proposal through serial communication.

allegations.summary: Whether the August 6 notice had to list a member's reopening proposal separately, since it was presented at the meeting without prior notice to the Chair.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee was not required to list Member Visnick’s proposal separately on the Committee’s notice for the August 6 meeting, as the Chair did not learn of the proposal until immediately before the meeting and therefore it was not an anticipated topic.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
